tool: Built-in image_gen; routine nearest-neighbor export to 240x240 with System.Drawing
frameA: Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: FM-1 hardware splash animation, FRAME A, ONE single frame only. Edit target: the supplied transparent PNG of the approved green/purple Crepuscular Homunculus. Preserve this EXACT creature, sinister smirk, narrow eyes, anatomy, pose, hands, feet, pointed ears, all existing skin bumps and pixel-art style. Do not redesign or invent a different creature. Make a square 240 by 240 pixel output canvas; keep transparency. Fit the COMPLETE existing creature, without cropping or distortion, into a region 160 pixels high and at most 160 pixels wide, horizontally centered, with its top at y=12 and feet no lower than y=172. This means the naturally tall narrow creature stays tall/narrow, about 101 pixels wide, with generous empty margins. Leave the bottom 50 pixels empty/transparent for a title to be added later. No text. Retain its source colors and sharp pixel-art shapes. This is the neutral animation frame, with bumps in their original positions. Output exactly ONE square PNG image containing exactly ONE creature. Do NOT output three characters, panels, comparison, collage, or sprite sheet. Transparent background.
b: Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: a SINGLE animation frame for the FM-1 homunculus. Edit target: supplied FRAME A square transparent PNG. Output ONE image containing exactly ONE character, with exactly the SAME square canvas and placement as the input. Preserve the input almost entirely. Lock ALL silhouette pixels, pose, size, location, hands, feet, ears, face, sinister smile, eyes, eyebrows, belly shape, lighting, background transparency, bottom blank space and color palette. Do not redraw the whole creature. Do not shift, scale, rotate, stretch or crop any part. Change ONLY four small interior skin bump highlight/shadow patches: a middle forehead bump above the eyebrows, the prominent outer shoulder bump on viewer's right, upper chest bump on viewer's right, and a belly bump. Surrounding pixels must stay unchanged. Keep pixel-art edges crisp and every changed patch within the skin. No text, panels, additional characters, extra objects, moving limbs, wounds, gore or overall color changes. FRAME B: show the existing forehead and chest bumps slightly more inflated: enlarge their pale highlight and dark lower rim a tiny amount. Flatten the shoulder and belly bumps slightly by reducing their bright centers. This should appear like subtle bubbling under the skin while the body remains absolutely still.
